# Personal Finance Overview

I spent a good chunk of the morning catching up on my finances. It's one of those things that always feels a bit tedious until it's done, then I feel so much better. I sat at the kitchen table with my laptop, a fresh cup of coffee, and my notebook where I jot down random money thoughts. The house was quiet except for the dog snoring on the rug. 

Lately I've been trying to get more organized with everything. Between work deadlines, the upcoming family visit, and just regular life stuff, it's easy for things to slip. That's why I decided to review all my accounts and goals in one go. I opened up my spreadsheets, logged into the various bank and investment portals, and started making notes about where everything stands.

## Retirement Savings

One of the bigger wins recently has been setting up consistent contributions to my Roth IRA at Fidelity. I've been putting in $300 per month automatically, which feels manageable with my current paycheck. It gets deducted right after payday so I don't even see the money sitting around tempting me to spend it. The account has been performing decently this year, though I'm not checking it every day. That was a bad habit I had before. Now I just glance at the balance once a month and move on.

I like the Roth option because the tax-free growth down the road seems smart, especially since I'm still in a relatively low tax bracket. Sometimes I wonder if I should bump it up to the full annual limit, but for now $300 a month feels sustainable. I added a reminder in my calendar to review this again in October before the year-end rush.

## Emergency Fund Progress

My emergency fund target is still sitting at 4 months of expenses, which comes out to about $9,000. I'm currently at around $6,800, so I've made good progress but there's still a gap. I try to add a little extra whenever I get a bonus or a tax refund. The money is parked in a high-yield savings account that actually earns a decent rate right now. 

It's funny how having that cushion has already helped me sleep better at night. Last month when the car needed unexpected repairs, I didn't have to stress about putting it on a credit card. I just transferred the money and moved on. Still aiming to reach the full $9,000 by the end of summer if everything goes according to plan.

## Credit Cards and Bill Payments

I made sure all my credit cards are set up with autopay on the 15th of every month. That's become my standard practice now after a few close calls in the past. The 15th works well because most of my income hits the account a few days earlier, so there's always enough to cover the balances in full. I've been religious about paying everything off each month to avoid interest.

While I was in there I also reviewed my recent spending categories. Groceries were a bit higher than usual because of that big barbecue we hosted, but overall things look on track. I need to remember to cancel that streaming subscription I don't use anymore. It's the little things that add up.

## Budget Review and Other Notes

The rest of the afternoon I spent tweaking my monthly budget categories. I increased the dining out allowance slightly since summer is coming and we'll probably eat outside more. I also made a note to look into whether I should open a separate brokerage account or just keep focusing on the retirement contributions for now.

Overall I'm feeling pretty good about where things stand. It's not perfect, but it's consistent. I scheduled a quick check-in for next month so I don't lose momentum. After I finished I treated myself to a walk around the neighborhood to clear my head. Money stuff always feels less overwhelming after it's written down and organized.
